Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
New Jersey Governor Mikey Sherrill has declared a state of emergency
for the state's coastal communities.
A nor'easter is bringing high winds, heavy rains, and major waves to the
region. In declaring the emergency, Sherrill urged people to take the
storm seriously and stay alert.
With this state of emergency, what that means is we will surge resources
to these communities, making sure that the Department of Environmental
Protection, the Department of Transportation are manning our operation
centers because of beach erosion and the high tide and the roads that
we are concerned about.
The storm is also affecting states as far north as New Hampshire.
Severe flooding is expected in some areas.
Residents of Hawaii's Big Island are preparing for what could be life
threatening flooding from Hurricane Nolo.
The National Weather Service says the tropical storm conditions are
expected to arrive there late tonight.
The hurricane could bring as much as 10 to 15 inches of rain along with
winds gusting to as much as 50 miles an hour.
And Hurricane Polo is now a category five storm off the Mexican coast.
It's expected to come on shore on the Baja California peninsula.
President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping wrapped up a state visit
Friday. As NPR's Emily Fang reports, they traded praise for each other but
did not address fundamental issues between the two countries.
While showing Xi around the National Archives, Trump told reporters,
"We had a great meeting." Meetings with Xi went great.
Trump also posted on social media that he will be heading to the
Chinese city of Shenzhen in November to meet Xi again and that Xi will
come back to the U.S. in December for the G20 Miami summit.
It's an ambitious schedule of in-person meetings between the two leaders
of two superpowers, but left unaddressed.
This visit were ongoing frictions of her competition in artificial
intelligence and semiconductors and rare earth minerals.
Nevertheless, at a state dinner this week, both Trump and Xi were all
smiles and toasted each other.
Emily Fang, NPR News.
The CDC's website now lists one death associated with measles as of
this week. As NPR's Rachel Carson tells us, the change comes during a
resurgence of measles in the country and after weeks of tension among
public health officials and the federal agency.
The tension stems from public health experts concerns about the CDC's
reliability. Pennsylvania reported four measles deaths so far in its
outbreak in the state.
When the deaths were first reported, Health Secretary Robert F.
Kennedy Jr. initially questioned whether measles was the cause and the
CDC removed them from the agency's website.
The single death now appearing on the site has an asterisk with a
footnote saying the number is subject to change after more reviews are
completed. It's unclear if this death is from Pennsylvania.
Nationally, there have been over 3,600 measles cases this year.
Rachel Carlson, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News.
Iran Friday said it would reopen the Strait of Four Moos and resume talks
on its nuclear program if the U.S.
agreed to several conditions.
Those conditions include lifting the U.S.
naval blockade on Iran, waving sanctions on Iranian oil sales and
observing a ceasefire that would include Lebanon.
All those conditions would need to be followed within seven days.
Ecuador says U.S.
troops helped hundreds of police bring down a dangerous drug trafficking
group and Pierre's carry-con reports.
Ecuador's interior minister says 50 U.S.
troops, together with 350 local police, arrested 39 people, bringing down
a local branch of the Mexican CJNG cartel operating inside Ecuador.
Earlier this week, Ecuador's defense ministry said the U.S.
military assisted in another operation, killing three, including an alleged
leader of the Choneros group. The U.S. has stepped up operations with Ecuador,
sinking six ships since August, which the U.S.
says were used to refuel speedboats transporting cocaine.
No evidence was provided, nor were arrests made, sparking allegations
of human rights violations.
Ecuador's President Daniel Noboa praised cooperation with the U.S., saying
the two are, quote, "working to recover Ecuador and the region."
Kerry Khan, NPR News, Rio de Janeiro.
A slowdown in oil prices helped to calm Wall Street
markets on Friday, and stocks closed out their first winning week
since early this month.
The S&P 500 added half a percent and pulled within seven
tenths of a percent of its all time high set last month.
The Dow Jones industrial's finished up by nine tenths and the Nasdaq
was up by half a percent.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
